articles.summary: 10-year financing to support ReNew’s under-construction renewable energy portfolio and deepen access to long-term international capital Gurugram, India; October 13, 2026: ReNew (“ ReNew ” or “the Company”), one of India’s leading decarbonisation solutions companies, today announced that it has secured a USD 100 million (approximately INR 955 crore) financing facility from FMO (Nederlandse Financierings -Maatschappij voor Ontwikkelingslanden N.V.), the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank. Extended to ReNew Solar Power Private Limited under the Voluntary Retention Route (VRR), the 10-year financing will support renewable energy projects currently under construction across the ReNew group. The transaction marks FMO’s largest single-ticket investment in India’s energy sector and its largest 2X-aligned corporate financing in Asia to date, underscoring the growing role of international development finance in supporting India’s clean energy transition. The facility qualifies under the 2X Challenge, a global initiative focused on advancing women’s economic participation and empowerment through investment. Proceeds from the INR-denominated financing will be deployed towards ReNew’s under-construction renewable energy projects. The long-term financing strengthens ReNew’s access to international capital and further diversifies its funding base across domestic and global markets. With a 10-year tenor aligned with the long operating life of renewable energy assets, the facility provides stable capital to support the Company’s expanding portfolio and continued growth. Kailash Vaswani, Chief Financial Officer, ReNew , said: “This financing is a strong endorsement of ReNew’s scale, execution capabilities and long-term growth strategy, and reflects the confidence of leading global institutions in India’s clean energy opportunity. The 10-year facility gives us access to stable, long-term capital at a critical stage of our portfolio build-out, while further diversifying our funding sources across international and domestic markets. We are delighted to strengthen our partnership with FMO and channel this capital towards projects that will contribute to India’s rapidly expanding clean energy ecosystem.” Marnix Monsfort , Director & Head – Energy, FMO, said: “We are pleased to partner with ReNew on this 2X-aligned investment and support the Company’s growth ambitions. As FMO’s largest investment in India’s energy sector, this transaction demonstrates our commitment to supporting India’s energy transition through impactful, large-scale financing solutions. ReNew has established itself as a leading renewable energy company in the country, and we look forward to supporting its continued contribution to India’s clean energy future.” The financing comes at a pivotal moment in India’s energy transition, as the country accelerates the deployment of renewable energy and the investment required to build the infrastructure of a low-carbon economy. For ReNew , the transaction reinforces its ability to mobilise long-term global capital at scale and deploy it towards projects that expand India’s clean energy capacity. It also deepens the Company’s relationship with FMO and reflects a shared commitment to financing an energy transition that is sustainable, inclusive and economically resilient. About ReNew ReNew is a leading decarbonization solutions company listed on Nasdaq (Nasdaq: RNW, RNWWW). ReNew’s clean energy portfolio of 20.5 GW (including 1.7 GW/6.2 GWh of BESS) on a gross basis as of August 18, 2026, is one of the largest globally. In addition to being a major independent power producer in India, we provide end-to-end solutions in a just and inclusive manner in the areas of clean energy, value-added energy offerings through digitalization, storage, and carbon markets that are increasingly integral to addressing climate change. In addition, ReNew has 6.4 GW of solar module and 2.5 GW of solar cell manufacturing capacities and is expanding its solar cells manufacturing capacity by another 4 GW, which is expected to be operational by December 2026. For more information, visit www.renew.com and follow us on LinkedIn, Facebook, X, and Instagram. Media enquiries: pr@renew.com About FMO FMO is the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank. As a leading impact investor, FMO supports sustainable private sector growth in developing countries and emerging markets by investing in ambitious projects and entrepreneurs. FMO believes that a strong private sector leads to economic and social development and has a 50+ year proven track-record in empowering entrepreneurs to make local economies more inclusive, productive, resilient and sustainable. FMO focuses on three sectors that have high development impact: Agribusiness, Food & Water, Energy, and Financial Institutions. With a total committed portfolio of EUR ~13 billion spanning over 85 countries, FMO is one of the larger bilateral private sector development banks globally. To get started, visit any supported model on Hugging Face and select "Customize and Deploy on SageMaker AI" or "Deploy on SageMaker AI," or click Get Started from the SageMaker Studio page. articles.summary: 10/13/26 Semrush Releases 2026 AI Visibility Index, Revealing Its First UK Benchmark Latest 2026 AI Visibility Index finds that the brands and sources surfaced by AI vary significantly between the UK and US — and that visibility on one AI platform does not guarantee visibility on another. Semrush, an Adobe company and the leading brand visibility platform, today announced the latest edition of its 2026 AI Visibility Index at Spotlight London, expanding its flagship research with a dedicated comparison on how major AI platforms surface brands and sources in the UK and US. The findings show that there is no single, global approach by which AI visibility is achieved. The brands that AI platforms mention, the sources they cite, and the level of consistency between platforms all differ by market. The new report analyzes seven months (January - July 2026) of AI visibility data across fixed monthly sets of 2.5 million UK and 25 million US prompts, built from Semrush search data, across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Google AI Mode, alongside a larger variable dataset of Google AI Overviews results for real search keywords. Across all seven monthly benchmarks, the four AI platforms agreed less in the UK than in the US on which brands to mention and which sources to cite. On average, any two platforms shared 63 to 70 of their top 100 mentioned brands in the UK, compared with 70 to 78 in the US. The study finds that Gemini mentions more distinct brands per answer than ChatGPT, while ChatGPT cites the most sources per answer of the four platforms studied. The result is a more fragmented AI visibility landscape in which brands need to understand their position by market, platform, and category, rather than relying on a single global ranking or approach. A strategy built for US AI answers may not transfer to the UK with the same results, and success requires a tailored, market-specific strategy to address each platform’s source mix and local domain signals like media, publishers, and communities. For enterprise brands, brand and AI visibility is a global concern. And with every additional market comes additional complexity. Brands need to optimize their own content for the audiences, questions, and expectations of each market, while also building the right third-party signals around them. -Marissa Dacay, Global Vice President, Enterprise Marketing, Adobe As the landscape continues to grow increasingly complex, the commercial stakes are also growing. Adobe data cited in the report shows that AI-referred visitors convert 60% better than non-AI traffic and generate 53% more revenue per visit. This underscores AI’s increasing role in consumer discovery, evaluation, and selection. Each Market Has Its Own Always-Visible Brands The Index identifies a persistent group of brands that appear among the top 100 mentions on all four AI platforms in every month measured — described in the study as the Universal Core. Twenty-four UK domain records met that standard, compared with 36 in the US, with only 15 domains shared across both markets, including Adobe, Apple, Amazon, Google, LinkedIn, Microsoft, Reddit, TikTok and YouTube. The UK-specific group is strikingly retail-led. Six of the nine domains unique to the UK Universal Core are ecommerce or retail brands: Amazon UK, Argos, Asda, eBay UK, Marks & Spencer and Tesco. BBC, Nike and TripAdvisor UK complete the UK-specific group. The US-specific set is considerably broader, spanning automotive, sport, entertainment and retail. The findings highlight how local brand ecosystems continue to matter even for global companies. A brand that is consistently visible in one market may have a very different AI footprint in another. AI is now a decision layer for customers, changing how they discover brands, sort through options and ultimately purchase. That makes visibility a business and commercial growth issue, not only a search issue. The sources and brands that shape decisions in the UK are not identical to those in the US, and teams need to build for those differences while keeping brands consistently discovered, evaluated and chosen wherever AI is shaping the decision. -Andrew Warden, Global Vice President of Marketing and CMO of Semrush, An Adobe Company UK AI Answers Rely More Heavily on News One of the clearest differences in the Index is the role that news and information publishers play across the two regions. In the UK, news publishers play a more dominant role in AI answers. On ChatGPT, news sites accounted for an average 29.5% of citations among the 100 most-cited UK domains, against 19.6% in the US. On Gemini, news was the leading UK source category in every month, at between 16.6% and 23.0% of top-100 citations. On ChatGPT, trip-planning sites and online marketplaces follow news in the UK, while online learning and streaming platforms follow it in the US. For brands, the findings reinforce the importance of third-party authority. AI visibility is shaped both by what a company says about itself, and what others say about it: publishers, marketplaces, communities and forums, and other independent sources. Those sources increasingly form part of the information layer AI systems use to answer user questions. Being Mentioned Is Not the Same as Being Cited The report also reinforces a central finding of the previous AI Visibility Index: being mentioned by an AI platform and being cited are two different forms of visibility. Averaged across 22 categories and four platforms, fewer than half of the top 100 mentioned brands also appear among the top 100 cited domains, in every month and in both markets. In the UK, average overlap across the study ranged from just 36.7 to 45.3 domains out of 100, depending on the month. The gap can be substantial even between direct competitors. In the UK, Tesco and Asda both remained among the top 100 mentioned brands across all four platforms in every month studied. Yet in July, Tesco ranked as ChatGPT's 25th most-cited UK domain, while Asda ranked 606th. On Gemini, the same two brands were considerably closer, ranking 29th and 60th respectively for citations. The example demonstrates why marketers cannot treat brand visibility in LLMs as a single score. Additional AI Visibility Index Takeaways Beyond the headline findings, the study reveals several important dynamics shaping how brands appear, compete, and build trust across AI-powered discovery environments: Each platform creates a different visibility environment. Gemini mentions more distinct brands per answer than ChatGPT, while ChatGPT cites the most sources per answer and Gemini the fewest. Google AI Overviews responses are particularly distinct. Across all seven months, brand mention overlap was consistently lowest in Google AI Overviews compared to the other three platforms. Its pairing with ChatGPT also has the lowest source overlap of any two platforms, in both markets. UK visibility is more fragmented across platforms. A larger share of leading UK domains appears on only one AI platform, reinforcing the need to measure ChatGPT, Gemini, AI Mode and AI Overviews independently rather than assuming performance on one has a correlating effect on others. Source concentration varies dramatically by platform. In the UK, AI Mode's ten leading source domains accounted for between 23.2% and 35.8% of citations among its 10,000 most-cited UK domains across the seven months, compared with only 12.8% to 15.4% for ChatGPT. Category matters as much as platform. The report finds meaningful differences between sectors including Real Estate, Finance, Industrial and Sports, requiring brands to benchmark themselves against the competitors and source ecosystem relevant to their own market and category rather than relying on a single global AI visibility benchmark. Availability The latest 2026 AI Visibility Index: Where the Top Brands Stand in the UK and US is available at https://ai-visibility-index.semrush.com/downloads/ai-visibility-index-2026-study-h2.
